thread:
PagerDuty: [P1] montclair-enterprise dedicated pool (pool-montclair-12) reporting sustained GPU utilization 98%+ and request queueing. Tenant: MontclairCorp. Paging SRE on-call. https://console.redwood/alerts/3223344556
Maya SRE: I'm on call, looking now.
Maya SRE: quick summary: queue depth spike ~420, tail latency >3s for generation endpoints, error rate ~0.4% 5xx.
Maya SRE: pulling per-tenant allocation and autoscale logs.
Julian (runtime): saw an alert in runtime too — KV cache growth + long sequences from Montclair's recent workload. Might be one heavy batching job.
Maya SRE: can we tell if autoscaler attempted to add nodes?
Ben Infra: autoscaler reported thermals OK; scale-up attempted but no spare capacity in the AZ due to other reserved pools. Autoscale hit quota limit: +0 nodes.
Tess CS: pinging MontclairCorp PM in parallel to verify they didn't kick a big synthetic workload. @Montclair contact says they launched a nightly bulk QA run unexpectedly.
Alice Support: customer impact = slow responses for production endpoints. They report timeouts for ~15% of requests in the last 10m.
Maya SRE: ok customer impact confirmed. Options: 1) approve manual burst from shared spare capacity (requires infra approval and billing override), 2) evict noncritical tenants on the node, 3) fallback to smaller quantized model for some routes, 4) ask customer to kill the job.
Julian (runtime): we can flip a routing rule to route MontclairCorp to a quantized model variant (gptq-8) which halves memory and cuts perf but keeps availability. Risk: output quality regressions.
Ben Infra: I have a spare 4-GPU host in eu-west-1 but it's reserved for infra backfill. Manual burst would need exec approval. Time to spin: ~90s once approved.
SRE_Bot: incidents: tag=montclair corp, severity=P1, runbook=/runbooks/dedicated-pool-gpu-exhaustion.md
Maya SRE: immediate mitigation — Julian, can you deploy routing fallback for 10% of Montclair traffic to gptq-8 as a canary? That should reduce GPU pressure.
Julian (runtime): yes. Pushing canary now. Command: ```rwctl route update --tenant montclair --target-model gptq-8 --percent 10 --reason "inc-3223344556 canary"```
Julian (runtime): canary applied, telemetry shows 10% routed, queue depth down ~18% in 60s.
Maya SRE: good. Next — Tess, can we request MontclairCorp to stop the QA run while we stabilize?
Tess CS: they acknowledged, asked for 15 min pause. They also asked if we can provide burst while they pause.
Ben Infra: I can request a manual burst for 20 mins from capacity pool. Need OOO exec sign-off for billing override. Who can approve?
Alice Support: Ops lead @Carla is online and can authorize short burst for customer impact.
Maya SRE: Carla approval required. Carla?
Carla (ops): approved one-time burst for 20m to avoid customer downtime. Please note billing will be adjusted. :white_check_mark:
Ben Infra: launching burst now. Spinning 4 GPUs -> attaching to pool (task id: burst-3223344556). ETA ~110s.
SRE_Bot: action logged: manual_burst by Carla for 20m, burst_id=burst-3223344556.
Maya SRE: while burst comes up, continue canary ramp if safe. Julian, ramp to 40%?
Julian (runtime): ramping to 40% over 30s. Monitoring.
Maya SRE: metrics: queue depth dropping, tail latency trending down to 1.2s, 5xxs falling.
Tess CS: customer confirms timeouts dropping, their production errors down to ~2%.
Ben Infra: burst host attached, pool capacity +4 GPUs. Observed immediate scheduler relief.
Maya SRE: propose eviction of noncritical batch tenants on affected hosts to avoid repeated cycles. Ben, can you identify low-priority tenants and evict gracefully?
Ben Infra: listing candidates: batch-job-alpha, nightly-backfill-7, analytics-staging. I'll drain them with 2m warning.
Ben Infra: evictions triggered. Command output:
```
> scheduler drain batch-job-alpha --grace 120s
> scheduler drain nightly-backfill-7 --grace 120s
> scheduler drain analytics-staging --grace 120s
```
Julian (runtime): canary now at 60% — system stable, tail latency ~0.9s, queue depth down 72%.
Maya SRE: great. Action summary so far: canary fallback (gptq-8) + manual burst + targeted evictions + customer paused job. That should hold.
Alice Support: customer impact mitigated. We'll keep them updated.
Tess CS: scheduling post-incident call with MontclairCorp for root cause and runbook change.
Maya SRE: monitoring for next 20m. If stable, we'll let burst expire and revert canary to 0% then re-evaluate autoscaler/quota.
Ben Infra: noted autoscaler quota issue — follow-up: request quota increase for eu-west-1 and add reserved buffer policy for enterprise pools.
Julian (runtime): will prepare a config change to make fallback model per-route configurable so next time it's automatic.
Maya SRE: final status at 3223344880: CPU/GPU pressure back to normal range, customer endpoints recovered. Closing the paging but keeping incident open for postmortem.
PagerDuty: Incident acknowledged and resolved (see incident timeline).
Maya SRE: filing postmortem and recommended actions: 1) quota increase request, 2) automated fallback policy, 3) customer education on bulk job scheduling, 4) billing flow for manual bursts.
Tess CS: adding follow-up meeting with MontclairCorp for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
Alice Support: marking support ticket #MC-7891 as mitigated.
Maya SRE: thanks team. :thumbsup:
